extra.message: The username and password taken from the POST /login/auth request body (routes/login.js:21-22) are concatenated directly into the SQL query string 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '...' AND password = '...'' and executed with db.one(). This allows SQL injection (e.g. username = ' OR '1'='1) to bypass authentication and dump the users table.

The 'id' query parameter from GET /products/detail (routes/products.js:47) is concatenated directly into 'SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = '...'' without parameterization, allowing SQL injection (e.g. id=1' UNION SELECT ...) to read arbitrary database contents.

The 'q' query parameter from GET /products/search (routes/products.js:67) is concatenated directly into the ILIKE clauses of 'SELECT * FROM products WHERE name ILIKE '%...%' OR description ILIKE '%...%'', allowing SQL injection to extract arbitrary data from the database.

All cart fields from the /products/buy request (mail, product_name, username, product_id, address, ship_date, phone, price — collected in routes/products.js:108-117) are concatenated directly into the INSERT INTO purchases statement, allowing SQL injection to insert arbitrary rows and manipulate or extract database data.

get_purcharsed() concatenates the username into 'SELECT * FROM purchases WHERE user_name = '...'' without parameterization. The value is req.session.user_name (routes/products.js:28), which is set verbatim from the user-supplied login username (routes/login.js:21,30), enabling second-order SQL injection.

The 'returnurl' query parameter (routes/login.js:12-14 passes url_params.returnurl to the template) is rendered unescaped with <%-returnurl%> inside the value attribute of a hidden input. An attacker can craft /login?returnurl="><script>alert(1)</script> to inject arbitrary JavaScript (attribute-context reflected XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The 'error' query parameter (routes/login.js:14 passes url_params.error as auth_error to the template) is rendered unescaped with <%-auth_error%> in the page body, enabling reflected XSS via /login?error=<script>alert(1)</script>.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The search query 'q' (routes/products.js:67,77 passes it as in_query) is echoed unescaped with <%- in_query %> in the results page header, enabling reflected XSS via /products/search?q=<script>alert(1)</script>.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Purchase record fields (product_name, mail, phone, ship_date, address, price) are rendered unescaped with <%- %>. These values originate from user-supplied /products/buy parameters (routes/products.js:108-117) and are stored in the purchases table, so an attacker can persist malicious script that executes for any user viewing /products/purchased (stored XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: After successful login the user is redirected to returnurl, taken directly from the POST body (req.body.returnurl) without any validation that it is a same-site relative path. An attacker can craft a login form with returnurl=http://evil.com to redirect victims to an arbitrary external site (open redirect, usable for phishing and credential theft).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The email-validation regular expression contains the ambiguous nested quantifier group (([-.]|[_]+)?([a-zA-Z0-9]+))* which exhibits catastrophic backtracking on non-matching input (e.g. a long run of 'a' followed by '!', as in attacks/evil_regex/attack_1.sh). Because Node.js is single-threaded, a single crafted 'mail' parameter to /products/buy blocks the event loop and denies service to all users.

The Express application is created and configured without any CSRF protection (no csurf middleware or anti-CSRF tokens anywhere). State-changing endpoints — POST /login/auth (routes/login.js:19) and /products/buy (routes/products.js:89), the latter also accepting GET parameters — can be triggered by an attacker-controlled page while the victim is authenticated, forging purchases and other actions.

The Express app never calls app.disable('x-powered-by'), so the default 'X-Powered-By: Express' response header discloses the framework to attackers, aiding fingerprinting and targeted attacks against known framework vulnerabilities.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: On authentication failure the raw database error message (err.message from pg-promise/Postgres, which can reveal internal query and database details) is passed to the client via the 'error' query parameter of the redirect URL, leaking internal error information to end users.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The express-session signing secret is a hardcoded string in source code. Anyone who obtains the source can forge validly-signed session cookies (e.g. setting logged=true) and impersonate any user. The secret should be randomly generated and loaded from environment configuration.

cwe: CWE-547: Use of Hard-coded, Security-sensitive Constants

extra.message: The session cookie is explicitly configured with secure: false, so the connect.sid session identifier is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections and can be intercepted by network attackers to hijack sessions.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The session cookie maxAge is set to 99999999999 ms (over 3 years), so sessions effectively never expire. This greatly extends the window for session hijacking, replay, and fixation attacks.

On successful authentication the existing session is reused (req.session.logged = true) without calling req.session.regenerate() to rotate the session identifier. An attacker who fixes a known session cookie value before the victim logs in retains a valid authenticated session afterwards (session fixation).

check_logged() redirects unauthenticated users to /login but returns no value, does not call next(), and does not halt processing; none of its callers (routes/products.js:11,26,43,64,91) check its result. Request handling therefore continues after the redirect — protected route logic (database queries and purchase processing) still executes for unauthenticated requests, making this a broken authorization gate.

Database credentials (postgres:postgres) are hardcoded in the source code connection string (repeated for the devel and docker configurations at lines 12 and 20). Anyone with access to the source or repository obtains direct database credentials.

Application user accounts with hardcoded passwords (admin:admin, roberto:asdfpiuw981) are defined in source code and inserted verbatim into the users table at startup. Hardcoded default credentials allow anyone with source access to authenticate as these users.

User passwords are inserted into the users table in plaintext (no hashing or salting), and do_auth (model/auth.js:7) compares plaintext passwords directly in SQL. A database compromise exposes every user's password in cleartext.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: The user-controlled username from the login request is written to the log file (app-custom.log via log4js) without any sanitization, allowing log forging/injection through embedded newlines, control characters, or fake log entries (demonstrated by attacks/log_injection.sh).

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
